drafts.title: fix(compiler-sfc): include extended call signatures in defineEmits type resolution
drafts.description:
Problem: In a component, defineEmits<ComponentEmits>() gets only the events that ComponentEmits declares itself. ComponentEmits extends BaseEmits. The events from BaseEmits are missing from the compiled emits option. In dev, Vue warns that the event 'input-event' is not declared. In prod, the extended events do not get set up.

Root cause: The function resolveInterfaceMembers in packages/compiler-sfc/src/script/resolveType.ts (lines 336-342) resolves each extended base type with resolveTypeElements. It then copies only the `props` field of the result into the child. It ignores the `calls` field. Call signatures such as (e: 'input-event', value: string): void are stored in `calls`, so the base call signatures are lost. extractRuntimeEmits in packages/compiler-sfc/src/script/defineEmits.ts reads `calls` from the resolved child. It never sees the base events. The bug is not in defineEmits.ts.

Fix: In resolveInterfaceMembers, take both `props` and `calls` from the resolved base type. Keep the existing props loop. Append the base `calls` to `base.calls`. Create `base.calls` when it is absent. Do not change any other function. Do not change the handling of the @vue-ignore comment or the error handling.

Scope: Only this change. No refactor. No change to defineProps behavior beyond what the shared code path gives.
drafts.summary: Decisions: (1) The root cause is in resolveInterfaceMembers (resolveType.ts), which drops `calls` from extended interfaces. We fix it there. (2) We do not change extractRuntimeEmits in defineEmits.ts. It already handles `calls` correctly for non-extended types and for union/intersection types (mergeElements already merges `calls`). Rejected: a workaround in defineEmits.ts that walks the `extends` clause itself. It would duplicate the type resolution logic and leave the shared resolver wrong. Rejected: a refactor of the resolver or extra tests beyond the one regression test. They are out of scope. Check done: no docs/arch directory exists in this repository, so no @arch keys apply. No open drafts and no ticket worktrees touch these files. The latest commit on main is a989345, and it does not touch these paths.

drafts.title: fix(compiler-core): resolve dotted component tag whose root is a prop
drafts.description:
Bug: in a <script setup> component, a dotted tag whose root name is a prop renders as an unknown element. Example: with `defineProps({ info: Object })`, the template `<info.icon />` renders `<info.icon></info.icon>` and not the component in `info.icon`.

Root cause file: packages/compiler-core/src/transforms/transformElement.ts. In resolveComponentType, step 3 handles dotted tags (`const dotIndex = tag.indexOf('.')`). It calls resolveSetupReference for the root name. The function resolveSetupReference ignores BindingTypes.PROPS and BindingTypes.PROPS_ALIASED. The lookup fails and the code falls to resolveComponent('info.icon').

Work to do:
1. In the dotted-tag branch of resolveComponentType, if resolveSetupReference returns nothing, check the root name against the prop bindings in context.bindingMetadata. Match the name, then its camelized form, then its PascalCase form, as resolveSetupReference does. Skip this check when bindingMetadata is missing or __isScriptSetup is false.
2. For a PROPS binding, return `$props.<name>` + the rest of the tag when context.inline is false. Return genPropsAccessExp(<name>) + the rest of the tag when context.inline is true.
3. For a PROPS_ALIASED binding, use the original prop name from bindingMetadata.__propsAliases. Non-inline: `$props['<original>']`. Inline: genPropsAccessExp(<original>).
4. Do not change the handling of undotted tags. Do not change resolveSetupReference behavior for undotted tags.

Out of scope: refactors, components without <script setup>, runtime changes, and docs.
drafts.summary: Root cause: packages/compiler-core/src/transforms/transformElement.ts, function resolveComponentType, step 3. For a dotted tag such as <info.icon />, the code calls resolveSetupReference on the root name 'info'. The function resolveSetupReference checks only SETUP_CONST, SETUP_REACTIVE_CONST, LITERAL_CONST, SETUP_LET, SETUP_REF and SETUP_MAYBE_REF. It does not check BindingTypes.PROPS or PROPS_ALIASED. When 'info' is a prop, the lookup returns nothing. The code then falls to step 5 and emits resolveComponent('info.icon'). The runtime cannot find a global component with that name. It renders the unknown element <info.icon></info.icon>. This matches the issue. In the reproduction (Vue 3.3.4), Comp.vue declares `const props = defineProps({ info })`. The tag <info.icon /> fails. The tag <abc.icon /> works because abc is a computed (SETUP_MAYBE_REF). The tag <props.info.icon /> works because props is SETUP_REACTIVE_CONST. Decision: in the dotted-tag branch of resolveComponentType, also resolve the root name when its binding type is PROPS or PROPS_ALIASED. Return the same prop access expression that transformExpression.ts uses for a prop: non-inline `$props.<name>` (PROPS_ALIASED: `$props['<original>']`), inline `__props.<name>` through genPropsAccessExp from @vue/shared. Append the rest of the tag (for example `.icon`) to that expression, as the existing code does for setup bindings. Keep the change inside the dotted branch. Options rejected: (1) Add PROPS to resolveSetupReference itself. That function also serves undotted tags. A prop named Foo used as <Foo/> would then stop going through resolveComponent. That changes existing behavior and the issue does not ask for it. (2) Tell users to write <component :is="info.icon" />. That is a workaround and does not fix the cause. (3) Support the same tag in components that do not use <script setup>. Step 3 is skipped for those components today (__isScriptSetup === false). The issue does not ask for it. No docs/arch directory exists in this repository, so no @arch key applies. No other draft is open (draft list is empty). The paths have no recent history except the HEAD commit.

drafts.title: Fix slot fallback/content swap when slot content uses v-if
drafts.description: Bug: A child component renders fallback. The parent passes slot content that uses v-if (for example content). When show toggles, the slot does not switch between the provided content and the fallback content. Root cause (from code reading; not yet confirmed by a run): packages/runtime-core/src/helpers/renderSlot.ts, function renderSlot, lines 63-78. The function creates one Fragment block for both cases. The key is `props.key || validSlotContent.key || `_${name}``. The key is the same string (`_default`) when the slot shows provided content and when it shows the fallback. The fallback is chosen when ensureValidVNode removes the v-if comment node. Vue then sees the same Fragment type and the same key, so it patches the old children in place. It does not replace them. The fallback children and the content children are not the same kind of node, so the in-place patch does not give the expected output. Fix to implement: in renderSlot.ts, make the Fragment key differ when the fallback is rendered. Append a suffix such as `_fb` to the key when `validSlotContent` is null and `fallback` is defined. Then Vue unmounts one branch and mounts the other. Change only this key expression. Out of scope: compiler changes (vIf.ts, transformSlotOutlet.ts), refactors, and extra tests beyond the regression test.
drafts.summary: Decision: fix the Fragment key in renderSlot (packages/runtime-core/src/helpers/renderSlot.ts). Rejected: changing vIf.ts or transformSlotOutlet.ts. The compiler already injects a branch key on v-if nodes, and the slot outlet path is not the part that loses the swap. Rejected: a workaround in the patch/diff code in renderer.ts, because the cause is the identical key that renderSlot creates. Rejected: a different fix such as always using a new key on each render, because that would remount stable slot content and lose element state. Caveat: the cause was found by reading code and by matching the known upstream problem (#7256, fixed after v3.4.29). The implementer must first write a failing test and confirm the failure before the change.

drafts.title: [Select] Forward the disabled attribute to the hidden <input> element
drafts.description:
Root cause: packages/material-ui/src/Select/SelectInput.js.

InputBase passes disabled={fcs.disabled} to its inputComponent (InputBase/InputBase.js line 432). For Select, the inputComponent is SelectInput.

SelectInput destructures disabled from props (line 38). It uses the value for tabIndex, aria-disabled, onMouseDown, and the disabled CSS classes on the display div and the icon.

Because disabled is removed from props, it is not in the `other` object. The hidden <input> (lines 397-407) spreads only `other`. So the <input> never receives disabled.

Work: in SelectInput.js, add disabled={disabled} to the hidden <input> element.

Out of scope: NativeSelectInput already sets disabled on the native <select>. Do not change it. Do not refactor. Do not add tests beyond the one in the constraints.

drafts.title: fix(system): run style() transform when themeKey maps to a function or array
drafts.description:
Problem: style({ prop, cssProperty, themeKey: 'spacing', transform }) never calls transform when the theme is present, because theme.spacing is a function.

Work:
1. In packages/material-ui-system/src/style.js, change getValue so that transform runs on the resolved value for a function theme mapping, an array theme mapping, and an object theme mapping.
2. Keep the fallback lookup (prop + capitalized value) in style() unchanged.
3. Add one test in packages/material-ui-system/src/style.test.js that shows the new behavior (see constraints).

Out of scope: refactors, changes to other system files, docs changes.
drafts.summary: Root cause: packages/material-ui-system/src/style.js, function getValue. The call to transform sits only inside the final else branch, where the theme mapping is a plain object. When the theme value at themeKey is a function (for example theme.spacing, which is a function in v5) or an array, getValue returns the theme result and never calls transform. This matches the issue: transform never runs when a theme is passed and themeKey is 'spacing'. The fix: apply transform to the resolved value in all three branches (function, array, object). Decision: change only getValue in style.js. Do not change the callers (borders.js, sizing.js, and others). Their transforms leave string results unchanged, so the existing border test with a function theme value keeps its result. Option rejected: a workaround with a custom spacing function outside style(). The issue asks style() to honor transform, so the root cause must be fixed. Option rejected: copy the stale PR 16439 commit. Reimplement the idea on current code, because style.js changed since then. No docs/arch blocks and no open draft or ticket worktree exist for this file. HEAD is 3506dda.

drafts.title: [useMediaQuery] Document that the first call returns defaultMatches unless noSsr is true
drafts.description:
ROOT CAUSE
File: packages/material-ui/src/useMediaQuery/useMediaQuery.js, lines 44-55.
The useState initializer reads window.matchMedia only when `noSsr && supportMatchMedia`. The default of `noSsr` is `false` (line 37). So the first call returns `ssrMatchMedia(query).matches` or `defaultMatches` (default `false`). The effect at lines 57-79 then calls `setMatch(queryList.matches)`. This causes a second render on each mount.

The hook cannot know if a hydration is in progress. The first client render must equal the server HTML, or React reports a hydration mismatch. The hook cannot tell a client-only app from a server-rendered app. A hydration detector is also not reliable with partial hydration. The issue author agrees: "no change is required to useMediaQuery".

The real defect is the documentation. It says the double render is for server-side reconciliation. It does not say that every client-only app pays for it on every mount until `noSsr` is set. It does not say that `noSsr` can be set for the whole app with the theme.

WORK
1. Edit only the English source docs/src/pages/components/use-media-query/use-media-query.md (API section, `options.defaultMatches` and `options.noSsr`, lines ~170-182).
2. State that the first call returns `defaultMatches` (or the `ssrMatchMedia` result) so that hydration matches the server. State that the real value arrives in a second render.
3. State that for a client-only app, `noSsr: true` makes the first call return the real `matchMedia(query).matches`, with one render.
4. Show how to set `noSsr: true` for all calls: `props: { MuiUseMediaQuery: { noSsr: true } }` in the theme. The existing note below the options already names the `MuiUseMediaQuery` key.

Do NOT edit use-media-query-{de,es,fr,ja,pt,ru,zh}.md. Crowdin generates them.
Do NOT change useMediaQuery.js, useMediaQuery.d.ts, or any test.
drafts.summary:
Decision: keep the hook behavior. Fix the docs.

Options rejected:
- Make `noSsr` default to `true`: breaks hydration for every server-rendered app. The first client render would differ from the server HTML.
- Add a `pastHydration` check in the initializer, as the issue sketches: the hook cannot detect hydration. Partial hydration can run it more than once. The issue author says this is not solved.
- Add a new global flag or provider for the hydration state: the issue asks for no new API, and `noSsr` through theme props already does this job. This would be extra scope.

Open point for the reviewer: the issue title says "bug", but the code matches the docs for `noSsr`. The issue body says no hook change is needed. If the maintainers want a hook change, this draft is the wrong scope. Raise it before work starts.
